title: Your giving
tomorrow: a fast nobody requires. why would Amira choose one?

segments.voice: Yesterday, my portion: a page you keep, stumbles counted twice. Today the portion is money, and the question is who gets to see it.

A fundraising page with a scrolling list of donor names, and a little box at checkout: show my name, or give anonymously. Some people click without thinking. Some hover over it for a while. Give quietly, or where people can see? The Qur'an speaks to that choice directly, and Muslims read it two ways.
screen: `SHOW MY NAME?` → `OR ANONYMOUS?` → `TWO WAYS TO READ IT.`

segments.voice: First, the plan itself. Zakat is the required giving: a set share of wealth above a threshold, owed by those who have it, for the people the Qur'an names: "The alms are only for the poor and the needy," the list begins. Sadaqah is everything beyond that: any amount, any time. A hadith even counts a smile as charity. Now the debate. In 2:271 the Qur'an says that giving openly is good, and that hiding it and giving to the poor is better for you. Two readings live inside that verse. View one: give where people can see. Its best case: giving spreads. A name on the list tells the next person this is normal, and some commentators say the required zakat, especially, can be given openly so others follow. View two: give in secret. Its best case: a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari names, among those God shades on the Last Day, a person who gives so quietly that the left hand doesn't know what the right hand gave. Secrecy guards the heart from wanting applause. A neighbor says nearly the same: in the Gospel of Matthew, Jesus says, "let not thy left hand know what thy right hand doeth." Both views give. They part only on the checkbox.
screen: `ZAKAT: REQUIRED.` · `SADAQAH: ANY AMOUNT, ANY TIME.` · `OPEN: GIVING SPREADS.` · `HIDDEN: THE LEFT HAND DOESN'T KNOW.` · then, large: `MY GIVING.`

segments.voice: Make a small giving plan in three lines. What you'll give regularly, even if it's small. Who it's for. And whether it goes out with your name or without, and why. Hold the plan in mind for the rest of the sit.
screen: `WHAT, REGULARLY.` · `FOR WHOM.` · `NAMED OR HIDDEN, AND WHY.`

segments.voice: Your giving: your plan for zakat, the required alms, and sadaqah, the giving beyond it. Open or hidden, it gets given.
Your line: my giving, planned before anyone asks, and kept whether or not anyone sees. Five of ten, given.
